- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment drop (e.g., -0.1×sentiment change).
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day after day 5.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.33/-0.33), model tends to misalign with true price mean — apply smoothing filter to reduce noise in forecast.
